[GENERATED IMPLEMENTATION]
import Lean.Meta.Tactic.Simp

def implementation (numbers: List Int) : Bool :=
let n := numbers.length
if 2 ≤ n then
  let rec loop i j : Bool := 
    if i = n then
      false
    else if j = n then
      loop (i + 1) i
    else if i = j then
      loop i (j + 1)
    else
      (numbers[i]! + numbers[j]!) = 0 ∨ loop i (j + 1)
  loop 0 1
else
  false
[END]
[HELPER LEMMAS]
[END]
[PROOF]
by
  unfold problem_spec
  let result := implementation numbers
  use result
  simp [result]
  simp [implementation]
  have h_spec := by
    -- We need to prove that the result is equivalent to the existence of a pair that sums to zero.
    have h_spec' := exists_zero_spec numbers
    simp [h_spec']
    split
    -- If there exists a pair (i, j) such that i ≠ j and numbers[i] + numbers[j] = 0, then result is true.
    intro h_exists
    simp [h_exists]
    apply And.intro
    simp [true.intro]
    simp [true.intro]
    apply And.intro
    simp [true.intro]
    simp [true.intro]
    apply And.intro
    simp [true.intro]
    simp [true.intro]
    apply And.intro
    simp [true.intro]
    simp [true.intro]
    apply And.intro
    simp [true.intro]
    simp [true.intro]
    -- If result is true, then there exists a pair (i, j) such that i ≠ j and numbers[i] + numbers[j] = 0.
    intro h_result
    simp [h_result]
